summary: Quick scoping call to align on pilot acceptance criteria and security/compliance gates. Primary asks: SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SSO (SAML/Okta) integration plan, RBAC and audit logs retention, KMS/HSM integration, and a two-stage benchmarking plan (functional quality + load). Agreed pilot outline: 6 week pilot, week 1 onboarding and baseline, week 2 baseline bench, week 4 stress/throughput bench, final acceptance by week 6. Next steps center on sharing security docs and running an initial bench using Vantage sample prompts.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-04 15:00 UTC — Duration ~52m. Attendees: Redwood: Maya, Diego, Anil, Priya. Vantage: Lena, Raj, Oliver, Sophie, Tom.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): okay hi everyone, thanks for doing this, I'm Maya from Redwood inference, i'm the AE on this account, uh joining with Diego and Anil on the technical side. quick roll call?
00:12 Speaker 2 (Lena): hey maya, lena here, this is raj, oliver, sophie and tom on procurement. thanks for setting this up.
00:18 Speaker 3 (Diego): thanks lena. goal today — make sure we align on security gates and the benchmark plan for the pilot. want to hear Vantage's acceptance criteria and any hard non-starters.
00:30 Speaker 4 (Raj): sure. from compliance perspective, SOC 2 Type II is must, and iso 27001 is preferred. also SSO via SAML (okta) obviously, rb- role-based access control with at least three roles, and audit logs retained for 1 year. data residency — EU for our EU customers, US for US. also need KMS integration or customer-managed keys, preferably HSM backed.
00:51 Speaker 2 (Lena): and from ML side we need throughput numbers — baseline token/sec for our typical payloads (we do long-ish prompts, ~1200 tokens average), plus p95 latency under 500ms for short prompts (<128 tokens). cost per 1k tokens is a factor but not a blocker for pilot.
01:10 Speaker 3 (Diego): okay good specifics. we can do SAML/Okta — that's standard, and RBAC + audit logs are in the platform. quick caveat: hosted api keeps ephemeral caches and has default retention that we can configure. for KMS we support both redwood-managed and customer-managed keys; for HSM we'll need an integration window.
01:34 Speaker 5 (Anil): Just to add, our dedicated and private options differ: dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools; private gives VPC/on-prem where control plane sits customer-side. both support SAML and KMS but private requires an onboarding window for networking + cert exchange.
01:53 Speaker 4 (Raj): what's the typical time to spin up a private trial? we have an internal change freeze late dec, so timeline matters.
02:00 Speaker 3 (Diego): private trial — usually 2–3 weeks to have an initial lab deployment (if your infra team is responsive), includes VPN/peering, KMS handshake, and audit log forwarding. hosted/dedicated pilot can start in days for simple API tests.
02:18 Speaker 2 (Lena): for success criteria, we'd like: 1) functional parity — same top-1 outputs on our test prompts within acceptable delta 95% of the time; 2) performance — p95 latency thresholds and throughput > X qps (we'll define X after we share sample traffic); 3) security — SOC2 + SSO + RBAC + audit logs in place; 4) integration — end-to-end advanced tests running in our CI.
02:38 Speaker 6 (Sophie): to clarify the "functional parity" — are we talking exact outputs? our product expects deterministic-ish behavior; small variation is ok if quality is preserved.
02:47 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes we look at quality metrics — e.g., BLEU is not quite right for chat; we'll use a prompt-level pass/fail and human evaluation on a 200-prompt subset. delta thresholds we'll define together.
03:00 Speaker 4 (Raj): on audit logs — what fields are in your logs? do they include request metadata, model version, tokens consumed, user id, and full prompt/response? we have privacy concerns about storing full PII in logs.
03:12 Speaker 5 (Anil): by default logs include metadata and model version; full prompt/response logging is optional and can be disabled or redacted. we also support field-level redaction and SIEM integration (syslog, splunk, S3 export). retention is configurable.
03:30 Speaker 2 (Lena): good. about KMS — we need envelope encryption. can you do EKM/HSM with AWS CloudHSM or Azure Key Vault managed HSM?
03:40 Speaker 5 (Anil): yes we support external KMS endpoints via standard APIs; HSM-backed keys are supported with some caveats around latency for key operations — we'll bench that.
03:50 Speaker 7 (Tom): procurement question — do you have SOC2 Type II report we can review under NDA? and can we get certs for encryption in transit?
03:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes we'll share SOC2 Type II summary and control matrix under NDA; we also have TLS certs and our transport is TLS1.2+ with modern ciphers.
04:10 Speaker 6 (Sophie): ok timeline — what's a realistic pilot duration? we want to go to production by Q1 if all goes well.
04:16 Speaker 3 (Diego): suggested pilot: 6 weeks. Week 0–1 onboarding and baseline data ingestion, week 2 baseline functional & small-scale performance bench, week 3 artifact changes, week 4 stress/throughput bench (sustained token/sec), week 5 tuning and RBAC + SSO validation, week 6 acceptance and SOW for production.
04:36 Speaker 2 (Lena): that sounds fine. on workloads: our median request is 420 tokens, average 1200 for some flows, concurrency pattern spikes to 200 concurrent requests for certain routes. we need batching strategy and KV cache behavior that doesn't blow latency for short prompts.
04:54 Speaker 5 (Anil): we can configure continuous prefix caching and dynamic batching windows. for short prompts we can pin a low-latency config and route to smaller-variance hardware. there's a cost tradeoff.
05:10 Speaker 4 (Raj): any data residency work required for EU users? we can't have EU traffic traverse US regions for certain data classes.
05:18 Speaker 3 (Diego): we have region routing. for hosted we'll route EU traffic to EU regions. for private you control cluster region. important: some telemetry/analytics may flow to centralized control plane, we can provide an option to opt out.
05:36 Speaker 6 (Sophie): benchmarks — what does your benchmark harness measure?
05:40 Speaker 5 (Anil): two parts: functional/quality bench (sample prompt set, human eval, pass/fail thresholds, hallucination checks) and load bench (latency distribution, p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec sustained, scaling behavior when we add model replicas). we'll provide scripts (jmeter-like) and an infra checklist.
06:00 Speaker 2 (Lena): can we run a light smoke bench within our test window next week? we want to see baseline throughput and initial latency numbers.
06:06 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes Diego: I'll drop the bench script and instructions to you. we typically need a 30–60 minute run to get representative numbers.
06:14 Speaker 4 (Oliver): about RBAC — we need roles: admin (full), developer (deploy/prompt configs), viewer (read-only). and service accounts for CI with token rotation. how are tokens rotated?
06:26 Speaker 5 (Anil): tokens support rotation via API and short-lived tokens for CI via OAuth flows. we also support JIT role assignment via SCIM for user groups.
06:35 Speaker 7 (Tom): procurement — pricing expectations for a 6 week pilot and a path to committed capacity?
06:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll provide a pilot pricing estimate and an incremental path to dedicated reserved capacity. typical pilots have a small weekly usage fee plus a refundable setup engineering fee for private. exact numbers in SOW.
06:52 Speaker 2 (Lena): can we capture acceptance metrics concretely now? I'll read them out and you confirm.
06:58 Speaker 6 (Sophie): yes please.
07:00 Speaker 4 (Lena): Acceptance metric A: functional pass rate >= 92% on the 2k prompt holdout set, with no major regressions vs our baseline. B: p95 latency < 500ms for short prompts and mean latency for long prompts < 2s. C: audit logs available with retention 12 months and redaction options. D: SAML SSO integrated with Okta and SCIM provisioning working. E: KMS integration with envelope encryption verified. F: throughput target — sustain 12k tokens/sec for peak route for 30 minutes without errors.
07:30 Speaker 3 (Diego): we can commit to those as long as we get the sample dataset and traffic profile. the 12k tokens/sec number — we'll validate during week 4 stress bench. there might be a modest config change.
07:45 Speaker 4 (Raj): one more security ask — can we have immutable audit exports to our SIEM and tamper-evident logs?
07:52 Speaker 5 (Anil): we support signed log exports to S3 and can configure SIEM ingestion. tamper evidence is available via append-only streams and HMAC signing. we'll share more details.
08:05 Speaker 2 (Lena): about PII — we'll share masked prompt samples. for any production-level prompts with PII we want redaction applied.
08:14 Speaker 1 (Maya): understood — we have built-in redaction and allow customers to pre-process prompts. we recommend a two-step: client-side tokenization + server-side redaction layer.
08:26 Speaker 6 (Sophie): does Redwood provide a SOC 2 mapping to controls we need to validate?
08:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, we have a control matrix. we'll send SOC2 Type II and an ISO 27001 summary under NDA.
08:40 Speaker 4 (Oliver): on network egress — if we do private trial can we restrict egress to only our internal endpoints?
08:46 Speaker 5 (Anil): yes, private deployments let you control egress. for hosted we can restrict outbound to specific endpoints but central control plane telemetry may be required; we'll document the exact flows.
09:00 Speaker 2 (Lena): how do you handle model version pinning and rollouts? we need deterministic outputs — pin to model sha and do canary rollouts.
09:07 Speaker 3 (Diego): model pinning is supported, and rollouts can be configured with weighted traffic or canary. we also support automatic fallback to compatible quantized variants when capacity is constrained.
09:20 Speaker 4 (Raj): any known limitations for enterprise encryption compliance?
09:24 Speaker 5 (Anil): main considerations are KMS latency and cert management; some HSM deployments need additional lead time for compliance reviews. otherwise we meet typical enterprise requirements.
09:36 Speaker 6 (Sophie): okay, let's recap next steps.
09:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): recap: we'll share security pack (SOC2, ISO summary, certs), SE to provide bench scripts, draft SOW & pilot pricing, and coordinate private deployment dates. Vantage will share sample prompts, traffic profile, and KMS endpoint.
09:55 Speaker 2 (Lena): agreed. any blockers?
09:58 Speaker 4 (Raj): none immediate, just need those artifacts and an NDA to review SOC2.
10:04 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll get NDA and pack out by Friday. thanks everyone.
10:10 Speaker 2 (Lena): thanks all, bye.
